title: Single tracer-based protocol for broad-spectrum kinase profiling in live cells with NanoBRET
author: Robers, Wilkinson, et al.

steps.title: Prepare HEK293 cells for transfection
steps.instruction: One day prior, passage HEK‑293 cells in DMEM + 10 % FBS (growth medium) ensuring they have not exceeded 50 passages; on the day of transfection confirm they are 70–90 % confluent, trypsinize, inactivate trypsin with complete growth medium, then centrifuge at 200 × g, 4 °C to obtain a cell pellet.

steps.title: Seed cells into 96‑well plate
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in Opti‑MEM + 1 % FBS and adjust the density to 2 × 10⁵ cells/mL; add 100 µL of this suspension to each well of a tissue‑culture‑treated 96‑well plate.

steps.title: Prepare DNA and Fugene transfection mixes
steps.instruction: Assemble all transfection complexes, including experimental kinases and controls, as follows:

substeps.instruction: a) For each analysis well prepare 3 µL of 2× Kinase DNA solution at 20 µg/mL (or 3 µL of 2× NanoLuc control vector diluted 1:9 with Transfection Carrier DNA, then diluted with TE buffer to 20 µg/mL). If DNA is frozen, thaw quickly at 37 °C and briefly centrifuge to collect liquid at the bottom.
b) Prepare 2× Fugene HD solution by diluting Fugene HD to a final concentration of 60 µL/mL in room‑temperature (22 °C–26 °C) Opti‑MEM; make 3 µL of this 2× Fugene HD solution per well.

c) Add equal volumes of the 2× Fugene HD solution to the corresponding 2× DNA solutions, mix on an orbital shaker for 15 s at 400 rpm, and allow complexes to form for 30 min at room temperature. (Experienced users may seed cells during this incubation.)

d) Include the following controls on each assay plate: Zero BRET control (NanoLuc control vector diluted as above), 100 % BRET control (Tracer + DMSO, no test compound), and a Transfection control (e.g., MET‑NanoLuc plasmid diluted in carrier DNA, transfected into at least four wells on a separate plate).

steps.title: Add transfection complexes to cells
steps.instruction: Transfer 5 µL of each prepared transfection complex into the corresponding well containing 100 µL of HEK293 cells (total volume 105 µL per well).

steps.title: Incubate transfected cells
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate for 16–24 h at 37 °C with 5 % CO₂; allow a minimum of 16 h for transfection, ideally 20–24 h.

steps.title: Prepare 3× NanoBRET substrate solution
steps.instruction: In a conical tube combine NanoBRET™ Nano‑Glo® Substrate diluted 1:166 and Extracellular NanoLuc Inhibitor diluted 1:500 in Opti‑MEM without serum or phenol red to give a 3× solution (final inhibitor concentration 60 µM, working concentration 20 µM). Mix gently by inverting 5–10 times; use the solution within 1.5 h of preparation.

steps.title: Add substrate to assay wells
steps.instruction: To each well containing transfected cells add 50 µL of the 3× Complete NanoBRET™ Nano‑Glo® Substrate with Extracellular Inhibitor, then incubate 2–3 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Add substrate to background wells
steps.instruction: To empty wells that are not adjacent to sample wells add 50 µL of the same 3× substrate, incubate 2–3 min at room temperature (use non‑adjacent wells to avoid signal bleed‑through).

steps.title: Measure donor and acceptor emissions
steps.instruction: Using a NanoBRET‑compatible luminometer, record donor emission at ~450 nm and acceptor emission at ~610 nm (or 630 nm) for each well.

steps.title: Calculate signal‑to‑background ratio
steps.instruction: Compute S/B as (donor RLUs from transfected cells + NanoGlo reagents) ÷ (donor RLUs from reagent‑only wells). Acceptable S/B is >1 000, ideally 1 × 10⁴–1 × 10⁵.

steps.title: Compute raw BRET ratios
steps.instruction: For each sample divide the acceptor emission value (e.g., 610 nm) by the donor emission value (450 nm) to obtain the raw BRET ratio.

steps.title: Determine fractional occupancy
steps.instruction: Calculate % Occupancy using the equation % Occupancy = [1 – (X – Z)/(Y – Z)] × 100, where X = BRET with test compound + tracer, Y = BRET with 100 % BRET control (Tracer + DMSO), and Z = BRET from the Zero BRET control (NanoLuc vector or kinase/NanoLuc fusion with saturating control compound).

steps.title: Create kinase dendrogram illustration
steps.instruction: Navigate to http://www.kinhub.org/kinmap/, click the “text” tab, enter kinase names (comma‑separated or column‑wise) using the required syntax, optionally edit symbols via the “help” subtab, click “plot”, then download the dendrogram image with the “download” button.
